methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: The "Time Binoculars" (Existence in Past)
content: Problem: Students confuse "It was" (describing a thing) with "There was" (stating that a thing existed in a place). They also forget to use "were" for plural nouns.

Solution: We introduce the "Time Binoculars". When we look at a place now, we say "There is/are". When we put on our Time Binoculars to look at an old picture, we must say "There was" (for one thing) or "There were" (for many things). We practice contrasting two pictures: "Now there are tall buildings. Then there were old trees." TPR involves putting hands like binoculars over the eyes when using the past tense.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show a picture of one old house. Ask: "What was there?" Student: "There was an old building."
S2 pull-out: Show a picture of many trees. Ask: "What was there?" Student: "There were many trees."
Communicative task: Information Gap (Section 8). "Time Detectives" compare a modern city map with an old village map using "There was/were" and "There is/are".

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W20: old, new, building, tree, river
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (old, new, building, tree, river) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: There was / There were (Past existence)
instructions: Grammar focus this week: There was / There were (Past existence).
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "The Time Detective Agency — The Old Town Mystery"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "The Time Detective Agency — The Old Town Mystery".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (old, new, building, tree, river usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

IN-CLASS SPEAKING ACTIVITIES — Session 3 (teacher-led)

Activity 1 — Pair Speaking (3–5 min, pairs):
  Student A: Give a past fact ("There was an old bridge").
  Student B: Give a present fact ("Now there is a new road"). Switch.

Challenge Extension (L3 — for advanced / older students):
  [O] L3 — Older: Fill in the blank with 3 options (10 items)
  There _______________ (was / were / are) a small village.
  There _______________ (were / was / is) small houses.
  There was a long _______________ (river / sky / apple).
  Now there _______________ (is / was / were) a new road.
  There was a quiet _______________ (temple / dog / car).
  There were many green _______________ (trees / building / water).
  Now there is a busy _______________ (market / sky / bed).
  The city is very _______________ (loud / quiet / happy) now.
  I _______________ (am / is / are) a Time Detective.
  We love learning about the _______________ (past / fast / last).
